logo.title: The Roofline M.
logo.lead: An M drawn as two East London gables, with a brick-red front door. It's the Meade initial and a terraced house in one mark. It sits in a navy tile that works as a sign, an app icon or a board topper. The wordmark is set in DM Serif Display.

story.title: Seventy years. Three owners. One name.
story.lead: Walter Joseph Meade opened on Hoe Street, Walthamstow, in 1953. Seven decades and only three owners later, W J Meade has five offices across East and North London and is still independent. The brand should feel established without feeling old: London stock brick, a navy front door and a firm handshake.
story.positioning: The independent East London agent with more history than any chain on the high street.

colour.title: Navy door, stock brick.
colour.lead: Navy is the classic front-door colour. London stock brick yellow (the colour of every Victorian terrace in E3) is the warm accent, and brick red is kept for the one thing that matters most: the valuation button.

type.title: Heritage serif, modern sans.
type.lead: DM Serif Display carries the "since 1953" confidence in headlines and prices. Inter Tight keeps property details, forms and small print crisp. Both are free on Google Fonts.

samples.label: Body 400
samples.text: Two-bedroom Victorian conversion, moments from Roman Road Market.

voice.title: Straight-talking and local.
voice.lead: Talk like the negotiator who's been on these streets for years: specific, honest and no agent-speak. Property descriptions must be accurate (Consumer Protection Regulations), so no puffery.
pairs: "Two minutes from Roman Road Market, with a south-facing garden."
"We'll tell you what it's really worth."

imagery.title: Streets, doors, daylight.
imagery.lead: Straight-on shots of East London terraces and front doors, bright interiors shot level, and the team out on the streets they cover. Avoid ultra-wide lenses that make rooms look bigger than they are. Buyers notice, and it costs trust.
